clue.text: Observe girl going round northern country

indicators.note: going round says the word for observe surrounds the abbreviation for northern

parts.note: to observe is to see
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: Someone watches a girl circling round to the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Observe' sits at the front as if it were an instruction to the solver; it is just the first piece, and 'going round' wraps it about the northern letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Senegal is a nation in West Africa, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Something bright and beautiful in tabloid — female sitting on cow!

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
to cow someone is to intimidate them, as does to lower (lour), meaning to look threatening or frown down

explanation.surface: A tabloid photo shows a woman perched on a cow.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'sitting on' puts F above LOWER. 'Cow' looks like the animal but is a verb, LOWER (rhymes with 'flower') meaning to scowl menacingly.
explanation.definitionFit: A big yellow bloom on a tall stalk is a bright and beautiful plant, echoing the hymn line about all things bright and beautiful.

clue.text: British granny eating a fruit

indicators.note: eating says the British granny takes in the single letter, holding it inside

parts.note: nana is a familiar name for a grandmother

explanation.surface: A British grandmother is munching on a piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' puts A inside B NANA, just after the B.
explanation.definitionFit: The banana is a long curved yellow tropical fruit.

clue.text: Tory literature produced by agreement

parts.note: Con is the short form of Conservative, i.e. a Tory
a tract is a pamphlet, a piece of printed literature

explanation.surface: Conservative pamphlets were produced by mutual accord.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract is a binding agreement between parties.

clue.text: One taking pictures gets rioter cavorting with champagne

indicators.note: cavorting means leaping about wildly, so the letters are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A photographer catches a rioter capering about with a bottle of fizz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cavorting' tells you to mix the letters of RIOTER and CHAMPAGNE together, all fifteen of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinematographer is the camera chief who shoots a film, someone taking moving pictures.

clue.text: Habits of those who are buttoned up?

definitions.text: Habits of those who are buttoned up?

parts.words: Habits of those who are buttoned up?
parts.note: habits are clothes, as in a riding habit, and buttoned up suggests reserved people but literally means a shirt fastened to the throat, where a collar and tie sit

explanation.surface: A question about the behaviour of reserved, uptight people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habits' seems to mean customs and 'buttoned up' seems to mean tight-lipped; read literally they are clothing and a collar done up at the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: Ties, scarves and collars are garments worn round the throat, the habits of a buttoned-up person.

clue.text: Dispute at home after trip in car?

indicators.note: after says the words for at home come behind the words for a car trip

parts.note: a run is a short journey by car
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out in the house following a drive.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-in is a quarrel or confrontation, a dispute.

clue.text: Holidaymakers needing celebratory drink — husband goes out

indicators.note: goes out says the husband's letter leaves the drink's name

parts.note: champers is British slang for champagne

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers want some bubbly while the man of the house leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Campers are people on holiday staying in tents or caravans.

clue.text: Explosive young reporter confronting a queen

parts.note: HE stands for high explosive
a cub is a novice journalist, a cub reporter

explanation.surface: A hot-headed young journalist faces up to a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Explosive' looks like it describes the reporter's temper; it is HE, high explosive.
explanation.definitionFit: Hecuba was queen of Troy in Greek legend, wife of Priam.

clue.text: Clegg gaining reputation — or Cleggy as that might be?

parts.note: Nick Clegg is the former British Liberal Democrat leader and Deputy Prime Minister
a name is a reputation, as in making a name for yourself

explanation.surface: The politician Clegg is building a reputation, or a pet name.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick Clegg led Britain's Liberal Democrats; 'Cleggy' is an informal label of the sort the answer describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleggy is a familiar tag made from a surname, an example of a pet label for someone.

clue.text: Like many an entrepreneur, feels terribly keen to get stuck in

indicators.note: get stuck in says the word for keen is pushed inside the scrambled letters
terribly signals the letters of the word feels are rearranged

parts.note: mad means keen, as in mad about football

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic go-getter feels very eager to roll up their sleeves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges the five letters of the first word to SELFE, and 'get stuck in' sets the keen word inside before the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-made person built success from nothing, as many business founders have.

clue.text: Season in which Bury will need width at the start

indicators.note: at the start says the width letter goes at the front of the burial word

parts.note: to inter is to bury

explanation.surface: In one season the town of Bury needs to widen at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a town in Greater Manchester, so the capital letter makes it look like a place, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Winter is the coldest of the four seasons of the year.

clue.text: View offered by girl interrupting parents

indicators.note: interrupting says the girl's name breaks into the word for parents

parts.note: Pa and Ma are both parents
Nora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A daughter cuts in on her mother and father to give her opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'View' looks like an opinion, but it is a wide scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A panorama is a wide, unbroken view of a landscape.

clue.text: A group of violent ravers, exceptionally cross

indicators.note: A group of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some unusually violent party-goers are very angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like an adjective, angry; it is the verb, to go over.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse something is to travel across it.

clue.text: Why does a dame ultimately look different? It's the cosmetic

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of dame
look different signals the letters are changed in order

explanation.surface: A woman wonders why an old lady looks so changed, and blames her make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives E, the end of DAME; 'look different' rearranges WHYDOESA plus E.
explanation.definitionFit: Coloured powder brushed on the eyelids is a type of make-up, a cosmetic.

clue.text: Refuse to go into a filthy place?

definitions.text: Refuse to go into a filthy place?

parts.words: Refuse to go into a filthy place?
parts.note: refuse looks like the verb, decline, but is the noun, kitchen waste, which is fed to the animals in a sty, a filthy place

explanation.surface: Someone declines to step inside somewhere dirty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as a verb, unwilling to enter; it is the noun, scraps given to pigs.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitchen scraps fed to pigs in their sty are waste food, refuse bound for a dirty place.

clue.text: Agreeable Conservative hurrying to embrace maiden

indicators.note: to embrace says the hurrying word wraps round the maiden's letter

parts.note: haring means running fast, like a hare
M is the abbreviation for a maiden over in cricket

explanation.surface: A pleasant Tory rushes over to hug a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a maiden is an over with no runs scored, recorded as M.
explanation.definitionFit: Charming means delightful and pleasing, so agreeable.

clue.text: House with good paintings? Here's original artist

parts.note: paintings are art

indicators.note: original points to the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A house full of fine pictures belonging to a pioneering painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'original artist' reads as a phrase, but 'original' picks H, the first letter of 'Here's'.
explanation.definitionFit: William Hogarth was an eighteenth-century English painter and engraver.

clue.text: Short introduction to crosswords is found in Chapter 1

indicators.note: found in says the opening pieces sit inside the chapter-and-one word

parts.note: the figure 1 is one

indicators.note: introduction to points to the opening letter of crosswords

explanation.surface: A brief primer on crosswords appears in the opening chapter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' puts CIS inside the chapter-and-figure pair; 'Short introduction' reads as one phrase, but 'Short' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Concise means brief and to the point, so short.

clue.text: One may account for current restriction

definitions.text: One may account for current restriction

parts.words: One may account for current restriction
parts.note: current seems to mean present-day, but it is electric current, and the device in a circuit that limits its flow explains the restriction

explanation.surface: Someone could explain a present-day limitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' seems to mean present; it is electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: A circuit component that opposes electric flow is responsible for restricting current.

clue.text: Revolutionary regions needing the installation of a governor

indicators.note: needing the installation of says the single letter is put inside the turned word
revolutionary signals the word for regions is turned round backwards

parts.note: parts are regions, as in these parts

explanation.surface: Rebel provinces want a new ruler installed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' turns PARTS into STRAP, and A goes in after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A satrap was a provincial governor in the ancient Persian empire.

clue.text: A convenience for people doing business

parts.note: a convenience is a public toilet, and the Gents is the men's toilet in British usage

explanation.surface: A public toilet set aside for business people.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a public convenience is a public toilet and the Gents is the men's lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Agents act on others' behalf in deals, so they are people doing business.

clue.text: Drink and dope upset you and me

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word for dope is turned upside down

parts.note: gen and dope both mean information
us is you and me

explanation.surface: A drink and a drug have made us both ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' looks like a drug; it is information, GEN, reversed to NEG.
explanation.definitionFit: Negus is a hot drink of port or sherry with sugar and spice.

clue.text: Old PM's forebear not half making a packet? Certainly not!

parts.note: Pitt the Elder and Pitt the Younger were eighteenth-century British prime ministers

indicators.note: not half says only the front half of the word for forebear is used

parts.note: a forebear is an ancestor

explanation.surface: An old prime minister's ancestor made a lot of money, supposedly.
explanation.walkthrough: A packet is British slang for a large sum of money, and 'Certainly not!' turns it to its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny, meagre sum of money is the opposite of a packet, a large sum.

clue.text: Nonsense about actress Diana being smug

indicators.note: about says the word for nonsense goes round the actress's surname

parts.note: pish is an exclamation meaning nonsense
Diana Rigg was the English actress of The Avengers

explanation.surface: Rubbish surrounds a self-satisfied film star.
explanation.definitionFit: Priggish means self-righteous and superior, close to smug.

clue.text: Stimulate love in an act of deception

indicators.note: in says the letter for love is placed inside the deception phrase

parts.note: an gives A and an act of deception is a ruse
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: Romance can be roused through trickery.
explanation.definitionFit: To arouse is to excite or stir up, so to stimulate.

clue.text: Artist's kettle?

parts.note: names a nineteenth-century American painter famous for a portrait of his mother, and a kettle that shrieks on the boil is one that makes a high piping noise

explanation.surface: A question about the kettle belonging to a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: The painter James McNeill Whistler lends his surname, which also describes a whistling kettle.
explanation.definitionFit: A kettle that whistles when boiling is a noisy device, sharing a surname with the painter James McNeill.
